newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:
* President Bill Clinton prepared to press Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on his promise to improve the lives of Palestinians when they meet on Monday.
* China finally seems to be taking action against and arresting compact disk pirates.
* Cosmologists are hopeful they will be able to find numbers showing the age, mass and fate of the universe, based on new observations and using new instruments.
* Bankers Trust has agreed to buy Alex. Brown Inc for about $1.7 billion in stock.
* Jack Kent Cooke, who in his life owned the Los Angeles Lakers, the Washington Redskins and the Chrysler Building, died at age 84.
* Thousands of computer operations could face serious systems glitches when the year 2000 comes.
* Women's ice hockey has gained international acceptance and will be an Olympic medal event for the first time at the 1998 Winter Games in Japan.

* Law-enforcement officials have started to install new sophisticated security devices which could lead to technology that would allow police officers to spot people on the street carrying concealed guns.
